page: Microsoft Azure F1als_v7 is a single-core virtual machine belonging to the Falsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 1 physical core, 1 thread, and 2.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The processor is equipped with 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This server does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provided.

Benchmark data highlights a strong contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded or memory-bound performance. The dedicated 4.5 GHz AMD core delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng and single-threaded compression tests, with gzip compression reaching 40.65 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 17.87 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% of benchmarks. However, due to the single-core limitation, multi-core stress-ng performance and Passmark CPU scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is also constrained, with a Passmark memory score in the bottom 10% and cached small-block read bandwidth in the bottom 25%, though uncached large-block read and write bandwidths maintain average tier performance at 39.33 GB/sec and 32.14 GB/sec respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F1als_v7 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring high single-threaded CPU performance without massive memory or storage footprints. The low memory density of 2.0 GB per core makes it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale multi-threaded applications, as reflected in its weak database and Redis benchmark results. However, its high clock speed and advanced vector extensions make it highly efficient for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, small-model text generation, and utility scripting where multi-core scaling is not required.
description: Microsoft Azure F1als_v7 is an x86_64 single-core virtual machine from the Falsv7 family, powered by a dedicated 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 1 vCPU, 1 physical core, and 2.0 GB of memory, with no local storage or bundled GPUs. The server excels in single-threaded tasks, achieving top-tier results in stress-ng single-core tests and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 compression. However, its overall multi-core and memory performance benchmarks fall into the lower tiers due to the single-core and low-memory constraints. Qualitatively, this server provides a cost-effective option for workloads requiring high clock-speed single-threaded execution rather than high memory capacity. It is best suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, and small-scale text generation tasks.
